speaker: Unknown
en: We already happen to have a CLI at YC that worked really well that wired a lot of systems together.
zh: YC 碰巧已经有一个运作得非常好的 CLI,它把很多系统连接在了一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: But anything that wasn't in there, we basically allow adding just arbitrary API keys
zh: 但任何不在这个里面的东西,我们基本上允许添加任意 API 密钥。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sort of thing.
zh: 诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also want to ensure that we have parity with just an employee working on their laptop.
zh: 然后我们还想确保我们与一个在自己笔记本上工作的员工具有对等的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So device code OAuth, we go ahead and ingest that into a keychain and then refresh it for you.
zh: 所以设备码 OAuth,我们直接把它摄取进一个密钥链,然后替你刷新它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's ideally supposed to imitate the experience of a person on their computer.
zh: 所以它理想上是要模拟一个人在自己电脑上的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: We mostly keep this to be read-only in the database, but we do allow for writes via human-reviewed bulk upstarts.
zh: 我们在数据库层面基本保持只读，但我们确实允许通过经人工审核的批量写入(写为 upstarts,原文如此)来进行写操作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the way that works is the agent will put forward a plan to edit the database that a person can kind of give a once over and ensure it's not doing anything crazy before the write actually happens.
zh: 它的工作方式是，智能体会提出一个编辑数据库的计划，人可以大致过目一遍，确保它没有做任何疯狂的事情，然后写入才真正发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing we've observed with this is that we've started just kind of rubber stamping these.
zh: 我们观察到的一件事是，我们已经开始有点直接盖章放行这些计划了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a little bit like I think if you guys use Claude Code in the early days, like you might have been reviewing the tool uses very closely and eventually you start to build up more trust in the agent.
zh: 这有点像，我想如果你们早期用过 Claude Code,一开始你可能会非常仔细地审查工具调用，最终你开始对智能体建立起更多信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is something that we're looking at very closely over the over the next few months.
zh: 所以这是我们未来几个月会非常密切关注的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so sort of like I was saying, the sandboxes in this system we like to think of as a resource for the agent, and less where the agent actually lives.
zh: 是的，就像我之前说的，这个系统里的沙箱，我们更愿意把它看作是智能体的一种资源，而不是智能体真正居住的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in QM, the agent can basically, by default, it's going to be using a particular sandbox, so that's going to be one that's been allocated to the user that it's talking to.
zh: 所以在 QM 里，智能体基本上默认会使用某个特定的沙箱，也就是分配给它正在对话的那个用户的沙箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in general,
zh: 但总体上，

speaker: Unknown
en: There are environments that the agent can kind of converge on and can collaborate with.
zh: 智能体可以汇聚并协作的环境是存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other key thing is that if the agent is working on like a heavier dev workload, it can go and reach for a machine that has more resources.
zh: 另一个关键点是，如果智能体在处理较重的开发工作负载，它可以去获取一台资源更多的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's working on something that's simpler, it'll just go for a sandbox that's less powerful.
zh: 如果它在处理更简单的东西，它就只会选一个性能较弱的沙箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so pushing that decision into the agent itself rather than the harness has been a really, really powerful thing.
zh: 把这个决策推给智能体本身而不是 harness,是一件非常非常强大的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Similarly, allowing the agent to tap into its own runtime.
zh: 类似地，允许智能体接入它自己的运行时。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically, if it can choose the provider that it's working with, you start to get out of situations like, I'm sure you guys have run into this with Fable.
zh: 基本上，如果它能选择自己合作的提供商，你就能开始摆脱一些情况，比如我确信你们在 Fable 上遇到过。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you try to do AI research, if you try to do cybersecurity, anything, you'll get a bunch of refusals.
zh: 如果你尝试做 AI 研究，如果你尝试做网络安全，任何这类事情，你会收到一堆拒绝。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we can do when the agent can control its own runtime, it can just pop out into another model when it needs to avoid a situation like that.
zh: 所以当智能体能控制自己的运行时时，它可以在需要避免这种情况时直接切换到另一个模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Similarly, like in the earlier situation, it's often useful to pop between different sandbox providers.
zh: 类似地，就像之前那种情况，在不同沙箱提供商之间切换通常也很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's something that we can do quite easily.
zh: 所以这是我们可以相当轻松做到的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a general rule, what we've tried to do is keep the harness extremely thin.
zh: 作为一个总体原则，我们一直努力让 harness 保持极其精简。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think of the kind of core of the system as being these three tools, where you have execution in a remote sandbox, reading and writing from object storage, and then publishing internal apps, a pretty simple sort of get backed system.
zh: 我们把系统的核心看作是这三个工具：在远程沙箱中执行、对对象存储的读写、以及发布内部应用，一个相当简单的 get backed(原文如此)系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we have other tools for interacting with memory and crons and that sort of thing.
zh: 然后我们还有其他工具用于与记忆和定时任务(crons)等交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we really think of these as sort of temporary
zh: 但我们真正把这些看作是某种临时的

speaker: Unknown
en: Papering over rough edges in the system.
zh: 用于糊住系统中粗糙边缘的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really the core of it is these three up here.
zh: 真正的核心是上面这三个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really try to keep it as small as we can.
zh: 我们真的尽力让它保持尽可能小。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we're sort of trying to be this like AGI anticipating harness, although since we aren't there yet, there are a few things that we've run into.
zh: 是的，我们有点在尝试做这种预判 AGI 的 harness,尽管我们还没到那一步，还是遇到了一些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of these is that the agents, we've tried to put them in this really capable environment where they have all these tools available to them, but they often give up way too early.
zh: 其中之一是，我们试图把智能体放进这个非常强大的环境，让它们拥有所有这些可用的工具，但它们经常过早放弃。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one thing we've experienced with, especially over the past month or so, has been setting, we call it like a grind tool, or basically we set budgets on goals.
zh: 所以尤其是过去一个月左右我们一直在处理的一件事，是设置——我们称之为 grind 工具，或者基本上我们对目标设置预算。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the agent is not allowed to give up on his task before a certain amount of like wall clock times, like a couple hours.
zh: 所以智能体在一定的真实时间(wall clock time)之前——比如几个小时——是不允许放弃任务的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or a certain amount of token spend.
zh: 或者一定的 token 花费。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what that can accomplish is just a lot better research outputs, better reports, that sort of thing.
zh: 这样能达到的效果就是好得多的研究产出、更好的报告，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's been really fun actually to see OpenAI and Anthropic crack some open problems in math with a very similar technique.
zh: 看到公开问卷和 Anthropic 用非常类似的技术破解一些公开的数学难题，真的很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it also works for just normal office work stuff too.
zh: 但它对普通的办公室工作类事务也有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that we've seen a lot of is, so this harness is supposed to work, it works in multiplayer, it works in Slack.
zh: 我们大量看到的另一件事是，这个 harness 本应支持多人协作，它在 Slack 上也能工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But because of the artifacts of its training, effectively, what we see is that the agent can get very confused about the situation that it's in, even if we specify this pretty clearly in the system prompt.
zh: 但由于其训练的产物，实际上我们看到的是，智能体会对它所处的情境感到非常困惑，即使我们在系统提示词里相当清楚地说明了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So having like local affordances for this has been something that's been really important.
zh: 所以为此提供本地的可供性(affordances)一直是非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, the other thing that has been a problem is that agents really don't understand social context.
zh: 是的，另一个一直是问题的事情是，智能体真的不理解社交情境。

speaker: Unknown
en: To make this a little more concrete, like if I tell Regan a piece of information, he intuitively sort of knows
zh: 说得更具体一点，比如如果我告诉 Regan 一条信息，他会直觉地知道

speaker: Unknown
en: Or at least has like a good mental framework of where it is okay to share that information.
zh: 或者至少对在哪里分享这条信息是合适的有一个良好的心理框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it takes some actual work to recreate this with an agent.
zh: 但用智能体重现这一点需要一些实际的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like privileged information can very easily just leak into these contexts where it should not be.
zh: 比如特权信息很容易就泄漏到它本不该出现的上下文里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the information that you can put in the brain is effectively like bounded by how good your permission system is.
zh: 所以你能放进大脑里的信息，实际上受限于你的权限系统有多好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so YC luckily has an existing software system with like fine-grained permissioning that has been built over the years, but a lot of people just don't have that.
zh: 所以 YC 很幸运有一个现成的软件系统，拥有多年来建立起来的细粒度权限控制，但很多人根本没有这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it takes work to allow for knowledge sharing in a nuanced way.
zh: 所以要以一种细致入微的方式实现知识共享是需要下功夫的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thanks everybody for listening.
zh: 所以感谢大家的聆听。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can try out QM, it's open source.
zh: 你们可以试用 QM,它是开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And coding agents are pretty good at standing it up.
zh: 而且 coding agent(编码智能体)很擅长把它搭起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you run into any problems, feel free to put up an issue and we'll look at it.
zh: 如果你遇到任何问题，尽管提一个 issue,我们会去看。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also hiring, so if any of this resonated with you or would be exciting, then feel free to send us an email.
zh: 我们也在招聘，所以如果这些内容让你有共鸣或觉得令人兴奋，欢迎给我们发邮件。
